extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, journalists, and policymakers interested in media, journalism and democracy (particularly Australian media)
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing the performance and democratic purpose of the news media (the 'fourth estate'), with emphasis on independence, accountability, investigative capacity, ownership concentration, ethics, and public trust in the Australian context.

rubrics_metrics.name: News media as watchdog of democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The news media is traditionally the watchdog of democracy and has a democratic purpose to hold power to account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how well media outlets perform the watchdog function: do they investigate and expose wrongdoing, inform citizens about public affairs, and enable democratic accountability? The book examines key news stories and journalists' attitudes to assess this role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalistic independence is a foundation for reviving the fourth estate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schultz argues for a revival of the fourth estate based on journalistic independence — assess the degree to which news organisations and journalists can operate free from undue influence by owners, advertisers, or political actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political autonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Political autonomy of journalism: the ability of the press to act independently from political control or capture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure whether editorial decisions and news agendas are kept separate from partisan or governmental pressures. The book pairs political autonomy with independence as necessary for revival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Increased accountability and responsiveness are required for reviving the fourth estate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess mechanisms by which media hold themselves accountable (corrections, editorial oversight, transparency) and how responsive they are to public concerns and civic needs. Schultz explicitly lists 'increased accountability and responsiveness' as part of the prescription for revival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative boldness
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism's boldness and investigative capacity: the extent to which journalism moves 'from reporting to investigating'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book notes Australian journalism 'has become bolder and more investigative' — evaluate frequency, depth, and institutional support for investigative reporting, and whether reporting challenges power effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialism versus public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The impact of increasing commercialism on journalistic quality and public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how commercial pressures (profit-seeking, audience metrics, advertising dependence) influence news selection, depth, and ethical choices. The page states increasing commercialism has impaired the ideal of the fourth estate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The level and trend of ethical standards within journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess occurrences of ethical lapses, clarity and enforcement of codes of ethics, and trends; the page states 'decreasing ethical standards have left the public sceptical.' Use examples of ethical controversies and institutional responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration of media ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which concentration of media ownership impairs the media's democratic role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate market structure: ownership concentration, conglomeration, cross-ownership, and their effects on editorial diversity, independence, and pluralism. The book identifies 'increasing concentration of media ownership' as a factor impairing the fourth estate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political, ethical and occupational interests as constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: How political, ethical and occupational interests within journalism constrain its democratic function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess internal and external interest groups (political influence, newsroom cultures, occupational norms) that shape reporting. The page notes these interests have impaired the reality of the fourth estate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public scepticism and trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Public scepticism toward the media as an outcome measure of media performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure public confidence and scepticism levels; the book links commercialism and falling ethical standards to public scepticism. Use surveys, trust metrics, and qualitative evidence about public attitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and clarity of the media's democratic purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The defined scope of journalism's democratic purpose and how clearly that purpose is articulated and pursued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether news organisations explicitly prioritise public-interest journalism, and whether their practices align with stated democratic aims. Schultz 'systematically analyses the role of journalism in Australia and the scope of its democratic purpose.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional legitimacy of the fourth estate
rubrics_metrics.description: The contests and challenges to the institutional legitimacy of the fourth estate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess legitimacy in the eyes of other institutions (government, judiciary, civil society) and the public; the contents list chapters on 'Contests to the Institutional Legitimacy of the Fourth Estate' which suggests evaluating claims and counterclaims about the media's rightful role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting and testing the ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: How the ideal of the fourth estate is accepted and empirically tested in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate both normative commitment to the watchdog ideal and empirical investigations into whether journalism meets that ideal. The book's chapters ('Accepting the Ideal', 'Testing the Ideal') imply assessment criteria combining normative expectations with case-study evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenging power
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism's effectiveness in challenging power structures and public authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess frequency and impact of reporting that challenges powerful actors; the chapter 'Challenging Power: Reporting in the 1980s' highlights evaluating historical and contemporary instances where journalism scrutinised authority.
